chunks: Aḥmad ibn ʿAbdūn informed me of it, from ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad ibn al-Zubayr, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥasan ibn Faḍḍāl, from Ayyūb ibn Nūḥ, from Muḥammad ibn Abī Ḥamzah, from ʿAlī ibn Yaqṭīn, from Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام, who said:
I asked about a menstruating woman who sweats in her garment. He said: If it is a garment that clings to her, then I do not like that she should perform salat (prayer) in it until she washes it.

key_terms.تَلْزَمُهُ: it clings to her or closely adheres to her body

ai.seo_question: Can one perform salat (prayer) in a garment sweated in by a menstruating woman?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning the garment of a menstruating woman when it is affected by her sweat. The Imam عليه السلام states dislike of performing salat (prayer) in such a garment when it is close-fitting or clinging, until it is washed, indicating a ruling connected to ritual purity and prayer etiquette.
